name: x402 portable conformance corpus
description: Recorded 402 responses with tool-neutral, three-dimensional expectations. See corpus/FORMAT.md. Assembled for x402-foundation/x402#3104.

10x402.note: the engine under test — worker/lint.js, 75 checks

@x402/core.note: the v2 client schemas every client-code citation in this corpus resolves against

x402.note: the v1 client package (x402 / x402-fetch), cited for v1 parse behaviour

x402-foundation/x402.note: main at the time this corpus was cut; every `spec` ref is a path in this tree

x402-doctor-prototype.license: NONE — the repository publishes no licence file and package.json declares none
x402-doctor-prototype.note: run from a temporary clone only. No file from this repository is vendored into 10x402, and no code from it is copied into the adapter: corpus/run-x402-doctor.mjs imports diagnoseX402Endpoint() from the clone at this commit and maps its output.

dimensions.payment: can the declared payment be interpreted and settled under the stated x402 version, per the normative specification?
dimensions.client_interop: will the cited client implementations parse and execute it correctly?
dimensions.discovery: will registry-specific metadata be accepted and indexed by the cited provider? (provider observation)

evidence_kinds.spec: normative — a section of the x402 specification at the pinned commit
evidence_kinds.client-code: binding for that client at the pinned version, and for nothing else
evidence_kinds.cdp-validator: observed behaviour of the CDP Bazaar validator — provider observation, not protocol
evidence_kinds.cdp-docs: CDP’s published seller documentation — provider observation, not protocol
evidence_kinds.field-report: a reproduced report from the x402 issue tracker
evidence_kinds.provider-observation: observed behaviour of a named provider or a live capture
evidence_kinds.house-opinion: this corpus’s own reasoning, cited as such. NOT normative and never to be read as one.

reason_tags.status-not-402: the unauthenticated request was not answered with 402
reason_tags.redirect: the 402 is reached through a redirect rather than served directly
reason_tags.free-tier-200: an unauthenticated caller is served 200 — there is no challenge to interpret
reason_tags.content-type: the envelope is served under a content-type that misdescribes it
reason_tags.envelope-absent: no payment envelope for the version in question
reason_tags.b64-urlsafe: the header is base64url, or otherwise outside the standard base64 alphabet the cited client validates against before decoding
reason_tags.b64-undecodable: the header does not base64-decode at all
reason_tags.envelope-not-json: the decoded payload is not JSON
reason_tags.wrong-version-field: x402Version is absent, or names a version other than the one the transport implies
reason_tags.version-crosstalk: a field or shape belonging to one protocol version appears in the other
reason_tags.missing-required-field: a field the version requires is absent
reason_tags.network-form: the network identifier is in the wrong form for the version (CAIP-2 vs bare name)
reason_tags.network-unknown: the network is well-formed but outside the cited client implementation’s closed enum
reason_tags.network-unsupported-by-provider: the network is valid and outside a named provider’s settlement set
reason_tags.amount-form: the amount is not a positive integer base-unit string
reason_tags.amount-below-provider-floor: the amount is legal protocol-wise and below a named provider’s indexing minimum
reason_tags.payee-form: payTo is absent, the wrong JSON type, or not an address of the network’s family
reason_tags.asset-form: asset is absent, the wrong JSON type, or not an identifier of the network’s family
reason_tags.timeout-form: maxTimeoutSeconds is absent or is not a positive integer NUMBER
reason_tags.missing-eip712-extra: no EIP-712 domain in `extra` on a chain whose scheme signs one
reason_tags.scheme-unknown: the scheme is outside the set the version admits
reason_tags.resource-shape: the resource is the wrong shape for the version (object vs flat string)
reason_tags.resource-url: the resource url is absent, unparseable, insecure, or does not identify the endpoint
reason_tags.dual-divergence: the v1 and v2 envelopes of one dual-stack response disagree on a payment term
reason_tags.bazaar-extension-absent: extensions.bazaar, or a required half of it, is absent
reason_tags.bazaar-info-schema-mismatch: the declared `info` does not validate against the `schema` published beside it
reason_tags.bazaar-schema-unresolvable: the schema depends on an external $ref a facilitator must not resolve
reason_tags.bazaar-input-shape: the declared input is absent or carries no `type` discriminator
reason_tags.bazaar-input-method: the declared input method disagrees with the verb the resource answers
reason_tags.bazaar-output-shape: the declared output block is malformed
reason_tags.bazaar-output-example: no computed output example is published
reason_tags.discovery-metadata: descriptive metadata a registry reads is absent or outside its bounds
reason_tags.legacy-v1-header-names: the response also exposes deprecated v1 header names
reason_tags.declaration-integrity: a declaration-integrity extension is present and does not describe this declaration
reason_tags.truncated: the tool stopped reading before the end of the input

fixtures.title: a v2 header padded with whitespace

evidence.ref: @x402/core@2.23.0 dist/cjs/schemas/index.js — the regex runs on the raw value, so a leading space fails it before decoding

fixtures.notes: Discovery is n/a on both base64 fixtures for the same reason: the envelope did not decode, so its registry metadata could not be judged at all — not a clean listing and not a refused one, an unanswerable question. THE FIXTURE THAT CANNOT SURVIVE A LIVE TRANSPORT. HTTP strips optional whitespace around a header value, so any tool that probes a live URL sees the trimmed header and cannot reproduce this at all. It is reachable only by linting a captured or pasted response — which is why the corpus carries the response rather than a URL. From the 10x402 suite — the client tests its base64 regex against the RAW header value and throws before decoding, so a header with a leading space is discarded unread. This linter used to trim first, which meant it validated a string the client never sees.

fixtures.title: the v2 envelope echoed into the 402 body

evidence.ref: specs/transports-v2/http.md § Response Body — "Response bodies are a server implementation concern"
x402-fetch@1.2.0 dist/esm/index.mjs:19-23 — a pre-header client parses the body with v1 rules

fixtures.notes: NOT A FAILURE ON ANY DIMENSION. A body that declares itself v2 is not a broken v1 envelope. 10x402 used to run the whole v1 core cascade over it and report five core errors about an object that never claimed to be v1. From the 10x402 suite — THE FIVE-ERROR CASCADE. A v2-only seller who mirrors their v2 envelope into the 402 body is doing something a v2 client never even reads — it takes the PAYMENT-REQUIRED header and consults the body only when there is none — but isV1Attempt() saw an object carrying x402Version and accepts[], ran the whole v1 cascade over it, and reported five core errors saying "this v1 envelope is missing a v1 field" about an object that had never claimed to be one. A body that declares itself v2 is not a broken v1 envelope. It is now one finding, at warn, that says exactly what it is.

fixtures.title: maxTimeoutSeconds as the string "60"

evidence.ref: specs/x402-specification-v2.md § 5.1.2 (PaymentRequirements table)
@x402/core@2.23.0 dist/cjs/schemas/index.js — z.number().positive(), no coercion, so "60" fails the schema
@x402/evm — where a quoted timeout slips through it is ADDED to a timestamp, concatenating rather than adding

fixtures.notes: From the 10x402 suite — THE COERCION THAT BLESSED A BROKEN ENVELOPE. The old predicate was Number.isFinite(Number(x)), which accepts "60", "  60  ", ["60"] and true. @x402/core types the field z.number().positive() and applies no coercion, so a quoted timeout fails the schema outright — and where it slips through, @x402/evm ADDS it to a timestamp, which concatenates instead of adding and produces a validBefore in the year 60000.
